newsitem.title: USA: Germany's Rexrodt sees 1997 German GDP up 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt sees 1997 German GDP up 2.5 pct.

text.p: Germany's Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Tuesday that he expects Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) to rise 2.5 percent in 1997.
"I still expect that we will make the 2.5 percent (growth goal)," Rexrodt told reporters before a round table discussion on financial and monetary affairs sponsored by the European Institute.
"The German economy is not in bad shape," Rexrodt said.
But Rexrodt added that Germany would take additional measures to meet its growth targets and deficit targets this year if necessary.
Forecasts for German economic growth are at the center of a debate over whether Germany will fulfill the strict criteria for Europe's monetary union.
Independent economists have said that Germany would need to post at least 2.5 percent growth this year in order to reach its budget deficit goal of 2.9 percent.
